newsitem.title: GERMANY: GERMAN COALITION STAYS UNITED ON REVALUATION PLAN.
newsitem.headline: GERMAN COALITION STAYS UNITED ON REVALUATION PLAN.

text.p: German Chancellery Minister Friedrich Bohl said on Monday after a four-hour crisis meeting with coalition leaders that the government remained "unified" on its plans to revalue Bundesbank assets this year.

Despite objections from the central bank, Bohl said that Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU) and the junior coalition partners, the Free Democrats (FDP), were determined to revalue the gold and currency assets.
Bohl told journalists outside the chancellery that Finance Minister Theo Waigel would state the government's position on the controversial plan in parliament on Wednesday morning.
"On the question of the revalution...we are still unified in our belief that this is right," Bohl said.

The conservative CDU/CSU and the centrist FDP said last week they planned to revalue the Bundesbank's gold and currency assets despite Bundesbank objections. Several deputies have since said they would not vote against the Bundesbank's will.
Waigel, desperate to fill budget holes in 1997 so that Germany can qualify for the single European currency, has to cope with a 15 billion mark ($8.8 billion) tax shortfall this year.
His plan to reap 20 billion marks from the revaluation of Bundesbank assets could partly ease the government's debt burden and help Germany meet the EMU entry criteria.
After the crisis meeting ended, Bohl said the coalition was still at odds over plans to fill budget holes, but that they were making progress.
He said there still could be problems balancing the 1997 budget even if the coalition could raise funds through an accelerated privatisation of assets.

The FDP has ruled out tax increases to fill the holes while media reports say Waigel wants to plug the deficit with petrol tax increases or a delay in the cut in the so-called solidarity tax for the reconstruction of eastern Germany.

Bohl said that Waigel, who will state the government's position on the controversial asset revaluation plan in parliament on Wednesday, would also discuss the proposed law on revaluation with the Bundesbank during the coming days.
